findings.title: Unfiltered Ground Texture Pixelation
findings.where: arena and road screens, entire background play area
findings.problem: The concrete and asphalt ground textures display severe, blocky pixelation and harsh, unblended tile edges, creating a stretched-low-res appearance.
findings.why: It destroys the visual fidelity expected of a modern WebGPU renderer, making the high-detail car sprite feel completely disconnected from its flat, muddy environment.
findings.fix: Apply anisotropic filtering, implement a detail map layer to overlay fine-grain noise at close distances, and use a multi-texture blend shader to break up the visible grid patterns.

findings.title: Over-simplified Vehicle Schematic
findings.problem: The preview schematic is a primitive, flat-shaded blue rounded rectangle with two plain squares, failing to represent the detailed post-apocalyptic buggy shown in other screens.
findings.why: It ruins the vehicular blueprint/assembly fantasy, failing to give visual feedback on where armor or weapons are physically mounted on the actual chassis.
findings.fix: Replace the basic rounded rectangle with a high-contrast wireframe/vector line-art illustration of the actual subcompact chassis, highlighting actual hardpoints (weapon slots, wheel arches, engine bay) when hovered.

findings.title: Low-fidelity Speedometer and Radar HUD Panels
findings.where: arena and road screens, bottom-center and bottom-left UI panels
findings.problem: The speedometer and radar containers are flat, opaque dark gray boxes with raw monospaced text and sharp corners, looking like debug overlays rather than stylized game HUDs.
findings.why: They draw the eye away from the action due to their solid geometry, breaking the immersive, rugged tactical theme of a vehicular RPG.
findings.fix: Redesign these panels with semi-transparent, scanline-textured backdrops, add industrial bevels or corner brackets to the borders, and style the speedometer digits with a digital segment display font.

findings.title: High-saturation Flat UI Icons in Overworld
findings.problem: The building interactive icons are flat, highly saturated neon chevrons (green, orange, blue, red) placed directly over 3D rendered buildings, completely clashing with the desaturated, grungy cracked-earth background.
findings.why: The visual language is inconsistent, mixing flat mobile-style UI markers with a grimy post-apocalyptic world, breaking player immersion.
findings.fix: Style the building markers as glowing holographic projections (using a scanline shader, additive blending, and a slight flicker) or rusted, physical signposts that fit the game's actual world art direction.

findings.title: Awkward Menu Box Spacing and Contrast
findings.problem: The menu box is surrounded by an overly thick, bright cyan outline with asymmetric padding around the raw list elements, leaving a massive empty dark-teal block below the second option.
findings.why: It looks like an unstyled HTML div template, immediately lowering the game's perceived production value before the player even starts playing.
findings.fix: Remove the heavy outer bounding box, align the interactive menu items directly underneath the subtitle with clean, left-aligned typographic markers, and use a subtle horizontal line separator instead.
